category_title: Middle school students with severe reading disabilities who disengage from traditional tasks
minimal_context: The student is tasked with organizing research and structuring writing for a short biography using a physical binder and notepaper in a classroom setting.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Please take out your physical binder and notepaper so we can organize your research and structure your writing for the short biography.

STUDENT: (Flipping through the binder) I don't know where my research is. I can't find the pages from yesterday.

TUTOR: Just look carefully through your binder.

STUDENT: They aren't here. I always lose my work when we have to use this paper stuff.

TUTOR: Well, you need to finish the assignment. Take out a new piece of notepaper and start over.

STUDENT: (Quietly puts his head on his desk, becoming 'invisible') I'm not doing it. I'm just going to lose it again anyway.

options.A: Implement a personalized intervention focused on instructing a replacement behavior that provides functionally relevant reinforcers.
options.B: Set a pedagogical goal to interrupt identity formation so they see themselves as writers through composing short biographies.
options.C: Use the Evernote app to take notes, organize their research, and archive past biography projects.
options.D: Engage in shared discourse and provide direct instruction in coping strategies within the classroom routine.
